declarations.description:
Form container around a native `<form>`: validation timing, an error summary, server errors, dirty tracking and
an async submit. Put one `<form>` in the default slot and wrap its controls in `c2-form-field`.

The native form stays in charge of its controls: `FormData`, reset, `requestSubmit`, `<fieldset disabled>` and
framework bindings work as they do without this element. On a submit attempt (a submit button, `submit()`), it
suppresses the browser's validation bubbles, shows every field's error, and either focuses the error summary (two
or more errors) or the one invalid control, then fires `invalid-submit`. When every control is valid it runs
`validator`, then fires `valid-submit` instead of submitting the page; `waitUntil` keeps the form busy while the
app saves.

Server errors (`errors`, `setErrors`, or a rejected `waitUntil`) show on the field whose control has that `name`
and clear when the user edits it. `necessity` and `validate-on` are the defaults of every `c2-form-field` inside.

The form is laid out as a grid of its children: `--c2-form--columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(220px, 1fr))` gives
several columns, and `--c2-form-field--grid-column: 1 / -1` on a field spans them all. Put the buttons in a row
container of their own.

The host exposes custom states: `:state(dirty)`, `:state(submitting)`, `:state(submitted)` (a submit was
attempted) and `:state(invalid)` (the last attempt found errors).
declarations.name: Form

cssProperties.description: `block` leaves the form's own layout alone.
cssProperties.name: --c2-form--display

slots.description: Replaces the summary heading ("There are 2 problems with this form").
slots.name: error-summary-heading

members.name: validateOn
members.description: When an error first shows, for every field inside: `submit`, `blur` or `input`. A field's own `validate-on` wins.

members.name: necessity
members.description: Marker style of every field inside: `required` (asterisk), `optional` ("Optional") or `none`. A field's own `necessity` wins.

members.name: errorSummary
members.description: `auto`: a summary above the form for two or more errors, focus on the control for one. `always`: a summary for one too. `none`: never.

members.name: errors
members.description: Server errors keyed by control `name`, e.g. `{"email": "Already registered"}`. Each one clears when its control is edited.

members.name: warnUnsaved
members.description: Asks before the page unloads while the form has unsaved changes.

members.name: validator
members.description: Cross-field and async checks, run once every control passes its own constraints.

members.name: form
members.description: The slotted native form.

members.name: values
members.description: The current values as a plain object; a name that appears more than once becomes an array.

members.name: dirty
members.description: True while the values differ from the pristine state (the authored values, or the last `markPristine()`).

members.name: submitting
members.description: True while a `waitUntil` promise is pending.

members.name: invalidFields
members.description: The errors found by the last submit attempt or `validate()`.

members.name: submit
members.description: Submits the form as a submit button would: validation always runs.

members.name: reset
members.description: Resets the form to its authored values and clears every error and the summary.

members.name: setErrors
members.description: Shows errors keyed by control `name` on their fields, as if the server had returned them. `{}` clears them.

members.name: validate
members.description: Runs every check without submitting and shows the result. Resolves to true when the form is valid.

members.name: markPristine
members.description: Takes the current values as the new pristine state, e.g. after a save the app did itself.

members.name: handleClick
members.description: A click on a submit button is a submit attempt: remember it, and which button it was.

members.name: handleKeydown
members.description: Enter in a single-line input submits implicitly.

members.name: handleInvalid
members.description: The browser fires `invalid` on every control that fails, before it would submit: one batch per attempt.

members.name: collectErrors
members.description: Every field's error, shown, plus controls outside a field that fail their constraints.

members.name: applyServerErrors
members.description:
Hands server errors to their fields. `replace` clears the fields an earlier call set and this one does not name
(the `errors` property is the whole set); a validator's result only adds.

members.name: refreshSummary
members.description: While the summary shows, entries leave it as their fields are fixed.

events.name: valid-submit
events.description: Every control is valid and `validator` passed. Detail: `{ formData, values, submitter, waitUntil(promise) }`. The page does not navigate.

events.name: invalid-submit
events.description: A submit attempt found errors. Detail: `{ errors: { name, message, control }[] }`.

events.name: dirty-change
events.description: The values started or stopped differing from the pristine state. Detail: `{ dirty }`.

attributes.name: validate-on
attributes.description: When an error first shows, for every field inside: `submit`, `blur` or `input`. A field's own `validate-on` wins.

attributes.name: errors
attributes.description: Server errors keyed by control `name`, e.g. `{"email": "Already registered"}`. Each one clears when its control is edited.

declarations.description:
A repeatable group of fields, the companion of `c2-form`: "Add another" appends a row cloned from a `<template>`,
and each row can be removed, duplicated and moved. The rows are light-DOM children, so their controls stay in the
native `<form>` and its `FormData`, validation and `c2-form-field`s work as for any other control.

Put the row markup in a `<template>` child; rows authored next to it are the initial rows. With a `name`, each
control's name gets the row's index (`name="email"` in the template becomes `contacts.0.email`), which keeps radio
groups apart and lets a server read the rows back; without one, names stay as written. `value` reads and writes
the rows as an array of objects keyed by those template names.

The list has no per-row buttons of its own: any element inside it with `data-action="remove"`, `"duplicate"`,
`"move-up"`, `"move-down"` or `"add"` does that to its row (`add` inserts after its row, or at the end outside a
row), and is disabled while the action is not possible (`min`, `max`, first and last row). The default `footer`
holds an "Add another" button. An element with `data-row-number` shows its row's 1-based position, for headings
such as "Contact 2".

After adding or duplicating, focus moves to the new row's first control; after removing, to the next row, the
previous one, or the add button. Changes are announced to screen readers. Resetting the form restores the rows the
list started with.

The host exposes custom states: `:state(empty)`, `:state(at-min)` and `:state(at-max)`.

cssProperties.description: Columns the list spans in a `c2-form` grid.
cssProperties.name: --c2-form-list--grid-column

cssProperties.description: Space between the rows, and before the footer.
cssProperties.name: --c2-form-list--gap

cssParts.description: The wrapper of the default slot.
cssParts.name: rows

slots.description: The `<template>` of a row, then the initial rows.
slots.name: default

slots.description: Replaces the default "Add another" button; an element with `data-action="add"` in it adds a row.
slots.name: footer

slots.description: Shown while the list has no rows.
slots.name: empty

members.name: name
members.description: Prefix of the controls' names: `contacts` names a template control `email` `contacts.0.email`, `contacts.1.email`… Empty leaves the names as written.

members.name: min
members.description: The fewest rows: the list starts with that many, and `remove` is disabled at it.

members.name: max
members.description: The most rows: `add` and `duplicate` are disabled at it. Unset is no limit.

members.name: addLabel
members.description: Accessible name of the default add button. Empty uses the `add` message ("Add another").

members.name: rows
members.description: The rows, in order.

members.name: value
members.description: Every row's values, keyed by the template's control names. Setting it replaces the rows, kept within `min` and `max`.

members.name: addRow
members.description: Inserts a row from the template at `index` (default: the end), filled with `values`. Returns it, or `null` at `max` or without a template.

members.name: removeRow
members.description: Removes the row at `index`, unless the list is at `min`.

members.name: duplicateRow
members.description: Inserts a copy of the row at `index`, with its current values, right after it.

members.name: moveRow
members.description: Moves the row at `from` to `to`. Focus stays where it was.

members.name: sync
members.description: Brings the rows to `min`, writes indexes into names and row numbers, and enables the actions that apply.

members.name: setPossible
members.description: Disables an action the list cannot do, and re-enables only what the list itself disabled.

members.name: owned
members.description: The elements in this list, not in a list nested inside one of its rows.

members.name: rowOf
members.description: The row a light-DOM descendant belongs to.

members.name: writeRow
members.description: Writes `values` into a row's controls; with `clear`, a control whose key is missing is emptied.

members.name: handleReset
members.description: The form resets its controls after this event: put the initial rows back first, so they reset with it.

members.name: activeElement
members.description: The focused element of the tree the rows are in.

members.name: focusFirst
members.description: Focuses a row's first control, else its first focusable element. Returns whether the row took focus.

events.name: rows-change
events.description: A row was added, removed, duplicated or moved, or the rows were replaced by `value` or a form reset. Detail: `{ action, index, from, value }`. It does not bubble; a bubbling `change` also fires so a surrounding `c2-form` sees the edit.
